items.rationale: The in-car impact is covered under 2.6.2 and 4.5.2, and the battery health waiver overrides the below-80% cutoff in 2.6.8. The supplier's report supports replacement under 7.1.10; an estimated €750 equivalent new unit less €50 in salvage gives €700.
Section 7.1.9 caps replacement at the pre-loss specification when an equivalent model is available. This line is solely the elective upgrade difference, so none of it is payable.

The cracked screen is covered impact damage under 2.6.3; under 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.10, an ordinary screen replacement with labour and testing is estimated at €180 gross. The tablet and laptop form one event under 2.6.4, and no deductible amount is stated.

Section 5.2.3 covers necessary examination of both affected units, including the uneconomic-to-repair laptop. At €45 per device, the €90 gross total is below the shared €250 event cap, assuming no invoice credit.
Under 4.2.6 and 7.1.5, a carry bag is covered only if it was itself damaged in the event. The invoice identifies no such damage, so none of the bag cost is payable.
Sections 3.5(f) and 7.1.8(e) exclude undertakings as to future performance, even when purchased with a covered replacement. No portion is payable.
Sections 3.5(d) and 4.3(c) exclude data recovery unless separately agreed. The battery health waiver does not grant data cover, so none of this charge is payable.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separate administration charges, including those from another provider engaged in the claim. No portion qualifies under Part 5 or Part 7.
